subject: English
title: Class 9 English Olympiad — Paper 5
instructions: The time allowed for this paper is 60 minutes.
This paper contains 50 objective-type (multiple-choice) questions carrying a total of 60 marks.
There is no negative marking for wrong answers.
Each question has four options; choose the one correct answer.
Section 1 and other regular sections carry 1 mark per question; the Achievers Section carries 3 marks per question.
Use of calculators is not permitted unless specified.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: The information ___ useful for the project.
Identify the correctly punctuated sentence.
Choose the antonym of 'ancient'.
Choose the correct word: Neither of the answers ___ correct.
Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, 'I am happy.'
options: He said that he was happy.
He said that I am happy.
He said that he is happy.
He said he will be happy.

questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'obscure'.
Choose the correctly spelled word.
Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: She runs 'quickly'.
Fill in the blank with the correct modal: You ___ finish your homework before playing.
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: She is afraid ___ spiders.
Choose the correct superlative form: This is the ___ book of all.
Identify the correctly written sentence.
options: Each of the girls has brought their own lunch.
Each of the girls has brought her own lunch.
Each of the girls have brought their own lunch.
Each of the girls have brought her own lunch.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: By the time we arrive, the movie ___ already started.
Identify the correctly formed question tag: They are leaving, ___?
Fill in the blank: The team ___ practicing hard for the tournament.
Choose the correct passive voice: 'The chef is cooking dinner.'
options: Dinner is cooked by the chef.
Dinner is being cooked by the chef.
Dinner was cooked by the chef.
Dinner has been cooked by the chef.

questions.question: Identify the error in the sentence: 'She don't like coffee.'
Choose the meaning of the idiom 'to break the ice'.
options: To initiate conversation in an awkward situation

questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'reluctant'.
Fill in the blank: Either the teacher or the students ___ mistaken.
Identify the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: My hobbies include: reading, painting, and swimming.
My hobbies include; reading, painting, and swimming
My hobbies include reading; painting, and swimming.
My hobbies include, reading painting and swimming.

questions.question: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: His ___ behaviour surprised everyone at the party.
Identify the correct reported speech: She said, 'I will visit you next week.'
options: She said that she visits me next week.
She said that she would visit me the following week.
She said that she will visit me next week.
She said I will visit you next week.

questions.question: Choose the correct conjunction: He was late, ___ he still caught the train.
Fill in the blank: She has been ___ for the exam since morning.
Fill in the blank: She has lived in this town ___ ten years.
Fill in the blank with the correct article: She is ___ university student.
Choose the correct plural form of 'child'.
Choose the word closest in meaning to 'diligent'.
Fill in the blank: If it ___ tomorrow, we will cancel the picnic.
Read: 'The teacher never raised her voice, yet the entire class listened intently whenever she spoke, respecting her calm authority.' What does this suggest about the teacher's approach?
options: Quiet confidence and respect can command attention as effectively as loudness

questions.question: Read: 'The librarian arranged a special reading corner for children, filled with cushions and colourful books, hoping to make reading feel like an adventure.' What was the librarian's goal?
options: To make reading an enjoyable and engaging experience for children
To reduce the number of visitors
To save space in the library

questions.question: Read: 'The young chef experimented with unusual ingredient combinations, believing that creativity was born from taking risks.' What value does the chef prioritize?
options: Creativity and willingness to take risks

questions.question: Read: 'The old clock tower had stopped working years ago, yet the townspeople never repaired it, treating its frozen hands as a quiet reminder of the past.' What does the clock tower represent?
options: A symbol of nostalgia and connection to the past
A source of town pride in technology
A sign of neglect and carelessness

questions.question: Read: 'The young entrepreneur faced rejection from ten investors before finally securing funding for her idea on the eleventh attempt.' What quality helped her succeed?
options: Giving up after the first rejection
Persistence and resilience in the face of repeated failure

questions.question: Read: 'Despite losing the match, the young athlete smiled and congratulated her opponent, saying she had learned more from this loss than any win.' What trait does the athlete display?
options: Good sportsmanship and a growth mindset

questions.question: Read: 'Aditi practiced the violin every single day, even when she felt discouraged, because she believed consistency mattered more than talent.' What quality does Aditi display?
Read: 'The old banyan tree in the village square had witnessed generations of children playing beneath its branches.' What does the banyan tree symbolize in this passage?
Read: 'The astronaut described seeing Earth from space as a life-changing moment that made her appreciate the planet's fragility.' What effect did this experience have on the astronaut?
options: It made her indifferent to environmental issues
It had no lasting impact on her
It made her afraid of space travel
It gave her a new perspective and deeper appreciation for Earth

questions.question: Read: 'The scientist's discovery was initially mocked by her peers, but decades later it became the foundation of modern medicine.' What does this passage suggest about the reception of new ideas?
options: Medicine has not changed in decades
Groundbreaking ideas are sometimes doubted before being recognized as valuable

questions.question: Read: 'Despite the traffic jam, Raghav stayed calm, using the extra time to plan his presentation in his head.' What can be inferred about Raghav's personality?
options: He is anxious and easily frustrated
He is resourceful and manages stress well

questions.question: Read: 'The hikers reached the summit just as the sun began to rise, painting the sky in shades of orange and pink.' What is the mood created by this description?
Read: 'Though the twins looked identical, their personalities couldn't have been more different — one was outgoing, the other reserved.' What contrast does this passage highlight?
options: Physical similarity versus difference in personality

questions.question: Read: 'The company's new policy required every employee to take a mandatory break every two hours, aiming to boost long-term productivity.' What is the underlying reasoning behind this policy?
options: Employees dislike breaks and this policy discourages them
The policy aims to reduce work hours overall
Regular breaks can improve focus and productivity over time
Breaks are only for relaxation and have no productivity link

questions.question: Read: 'Before every match, the coach reminded the team that losing gracefully was as important as winning.' What value is the coach emphasizing?
options: Sportsmanship and humility in both victory and defeat

questions.question: Read the two statements: (1) 'She rarely makes mistakes.' (2) 'She almost always gets things right.' What is the relationship between them?
options: Statement 1 is much stronger than statement 2
They convey a similar meaning in different words

questions.question: A student must summarize a two-page article into a single sentence without losing its central argument. What skill is primarily being tested?
options: Concise synthesis of the main idea

questions.question: A paragraph inconsistently switches between first-person ('I') and third-person ('she') when referring to the same character. What editing principle addresses this?
options: Maintaining a consistent narrative point of view throughout

questions.question: Which sentence best uses personification to describe the wind?
options: 'The wind whispered secrets through the trees.'
'The wind was recorded by the weather station.'

questions.question: Which sentence demonstrates the most effective use of a rhetorical question to engage a reader on environmental conservation?
options: 'If we don't act now to protect our forests, what will be left for future generations?'
'Forests cover a certain percentage of the Earth.'
'Some forests are large and some are small.'
